(a) Findings.—Section 2 of the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996 (50 U.S.C. 1701 note) is amended by striking paragraph (4). 
    (b) Declaration of Policy.—Section 3 of the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996 (50 U.S.C. 1701 note) is amended—
        (1) in subsection (a), by striking “(a) Policy With Respect to Iran.—”; and 
        (2) by striking subsection (b).  
    (c) Termination of Sanctions.—Section 8 of the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996 (50 U.S.C. 1701 note) is amended—
        (1) in subsection (a), by striking “(a) Iran.—”; and 
        (2) by striking subsection (b).  
    (d) Duration of Sanctions; Presidential Waiver.—Section 9(c)(2)(C) of the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996 (50 U.S.C. 1701 note) is amended to read as follows:“(C) an estimate of the significance of the provision of the items described in section 5(a) or section 5(b) to Iran’s ability to, respectively, develop its petroleum resources or its weapons of mass destruction or other military capabilities; and”. 
    (e) Reports Required.—Section 10(b)(1) of the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996 (50 U.S.C. 1701 note) is amended by striking “and Libya” each place it appears. 
    (f) Definitions.—Section 14 of the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996 (50 U.S.C. 1701 note) is amended—
        (1) in paragraph (9)—
            (A) in the matter preceding subparagraph (A), by—
                (i) striking “, or with the Government of Libya or a nongovernmental entity in Libya,”; and 
                (ii) by striking “nongovenmental” and inserting “nongovernmental”; and  
            (B) in subparagraph (A), by striking “or Libya (as the case may be)”;  
        (2) by striking paragraph (12); and 
        (3) by redesignating paragraphs (13), (14), (15), (16), and (17) as paragraphs (12), (13), (14), (15), and (16), respectively.  
    (g) Short Title.—
        (1) In general.—Section 1 of the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996 (50 U.S.C. 1701 note) is amended by striking “and Libya”. 
        (2) References.—Any reference in any other provision of law, regulation, document, or other record of the United States to the “Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996” shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Iran Sanctions Act of 1996”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the headings "Reports Required" and "Presidential Waiver" signal a consultative process. But the section only makes technical conforming amendments that remove references to Libya from the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act and rename it. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue, and any reports referenced go to Congress, which is inside the federal government.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996, primarily removing references to Libya and renaming the act. It does not establish any new process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The text describes legislative changes to existing statutes rather than creating a mechanism for external participation in federal decision-making.

opus.w: The section only makes technical amendments that remove references to Libya from the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act and rename it the Iran Sanctions Act. Headings like "Reports Required" and "Presidential Waiver" might suggest a process, but any reports go to Congress, which is inside the federal government. The waiver stays within the executive branch. No comment period, hearing, outside advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue is created.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996, including striking specific paragraphs, redefining terms, and updating short titles. It does not create any new mechanisms for public participation, such as comment periods, hearings, or advisory committees involving non-federal parties. The references to 'nongovernmental entities' are within the context of defining who is subject to sanctions, not who participates in the regulatory decision-making process.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the statute amends laws affecting foreign entities (Iran, Libya) and mentions "nongovernmental entities," it involves outside parties. However, the text itself only describes legislative amendments, definitions, and reporting requirements. It does not establish a process for those outside entities to participate in the decision-making process (e.g., no comment periods, hearings, or advisory boards are created or mandated in this specific text). The "nongovernmental entity" mention is part of a definition being amended, not a participation mechanism.
